blanks.sentence: A food eaten regularly by many people can be called a _____.
Rice farming is under pressure from droughts and floods linked to _____.
Around four billion people depend on rice as their _____.
Brown, long-grained and basmati rice are examples of rice _____.
Current research aims to improve rice’s environmental _____.
The new farming method is called _____.
In AWD, measuring pipes are installed _____.
One target of AWD is methane-emission _____.
Farmers were worried that trying AWD might reduce their _____.
Besides saving resources, the amount of rice produced also _____.

multipleChoice.question: What does Dr Pinto emphasise about rice?
options: It is mainly a luxury food in Europe.
It feeds a very large share of the global population.
It is grown only in South and Southeast Asia.
It has recently stopped being popular in Africa.

multipleChoice.question: What is a major aim of current rice research?
options: To make rice depend on constant flooding only.
To remove traditional rice varieties from farms.
To reduce demand for rice in Asia.
To develop rice that copes with water extremes.

multipleChoice.question: What does “appetite” mean in this part of the discussion?
options: A strong global demand for rice.
A physical hunger caused by rice farming.
A preference only for basmati rice.
A decrease in rice consumption worldwide.

multipleChoice.question: What is presented as a possible way to make rice farming greener?
options: Growing rice only in Europe.
Replacing rice with potatoes.
Using a method called Alternate Wet Drying.
Flooding paddies more often than before.

multipleChoice.question: Why are measuring pipes used in AWD?
options: To keep the paddies flooded permanently.
To let farmers monitor field water levels.
To measure the amount of rice sold.
To increase methane emissions deliberately.

multipleChoice.question: What happened in the AWD experiment mentioned?
options: Over a thousand farmers used the method to cut methane emissions.
Only a few farmers tested AWD without clear targets.
Farmers used AWD mainly to increase water use.
The technique was tested without involving farmers.

multipleChoice.question: Why were some farmers hesitant about AWD?
options: They did not understand what rice was used for.
They preferred to grow only European rice varieties.
They wanted more floods caused by climate change.
They feared losing income from their crops.

multipleChoice.question: What would help persuade farmers to keep using AWD?
options: A promise that no measurements are needed.
A guarantee that rice farming will stop.
Clear evidence of better results after harvest.
Proof that methane emissions are irrelevant.

multipleChoice.question: What was the overall result of using AWD?
options: It saved water but reduced rice output.
It improved efficiency, emissions and yield at the same time.
It helped farmers only by increasing electricity use.
It had no measurable impact after harvest.

multipleChoice.question: What can be inferred about AWD from the final outcome?
options: It is useful only when farmers accept lower yields.
It solves climate change completely.
It works by making rice a less popular food.
It can offer both environmental and practical farming benefits.
